name: Minz Zhuang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only refs found are Johnson & Wang 2008 sociolinguistic survey and Pittayaporn 2009 (comparative); no phonology of Minz Zhuang located.

sources.citation: Jackson, Emily H. S., Eric M. Jackson and Lau Shuh Huey. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Dejing Zhuang Dialect Area. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-036. 168 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (the only 'stress' token is psychological stress of RTT participants). Contains tone-category correspondence tables for Napo Min (敏, D06) vs Jingxi Yang and Napo Yangzhou (tables 22-23) and wordlist edit-distance results; proposes extending [zgm] to Guangxi 'Min-Zong'.

sources.citation: Johnson, Eric C. 2011. A Lexical and Phonological Comparison of the Central Taic Languages of Wenshan Prefecture, China: Getting More Out of Language Survey Wordlists Than Just Lexical Similarity Percentages. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2011-005. 171 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives Balong Min Zhuang tone system (sec. 3.2.5-3.2.6, printed pp. 38-44: six tones 35, 33, 11, 31, 22, 55) and Proto-Tai > Nong/Min initial and rhyme reflexes (3.4-3.6); p.110 states allophony incl. tone sandhi, morphophonology and intonation are outside its scope. Only 'accent' hit is Li 1977's accent on the first element of PT diphthongs (p.~103).

sources.citation: Johnson, Eric C. 2010. A Sociolinguistic Introduction to the Central Taic Languages of Wenshan Prefecture, China. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2010-027. 114 pp.

sources.note: Jackson et al. 2012 report that the Dejing-area county almanacs give tone values and brief phonological notes for local Zhuang varieties; Napo is where the Guangxi Min (敏话) villages are, so its language chapter is the likeliest Chinese-language sketch of Min; whether it mentions 重音/轻声 is unknown.
